approvalTitle: design.md: converting the C4 diagrams (proposes amendments to finding A5 and requirement 2.2)
content:
# Design Document ## Overview C4 is converted in **two stages**, because the approved requirements stand at the default of Q5: *derive first, read later*. This document designs the first stage in full, as **ten steps, each one pull request, each held to one frozen transcript**, and says in one section (*What waits, and on what*) what the second stage is and which language change each part of it needs. The first stage ends in the shape the timeline has today: the palette, the menus, the rows, the findings, the drawn lines, the title and the legend come from six bundled DISL definitions, and the body is still read by `C4Parser` and written by the module's commands. Three classes carry it: - `C4Definitions`: the six bundled definitions, loaded once, found by origin, and what the providers derive from the one a view is drawn by, mapped to today's wire ids by its `x-c4` block. - `C4Disl`: the DISL model of one parsed workspace for one view, built from `C4Parser`'s reading. It is the stand-in Q5 names, for gaps C1, C2 and C6, and it is deleted when FBL reads the body. - `C4FindingOrder`: today's order of findings, by element. It is the stand-in Q4 names, for gap C10. Nothing a user sees changes in this stage except the two empty-canvas labels of finding A14, fixed on purpose in a step of its own. **Two points of the approved requirements are proposed for a small amendment** before the tasks are written, in *Amendment proposed* below. Neither changes what the tool does. ## Steering Document Alignment ### Technical Standards (tech.md) - *Specifying a diagram type*: the six definitions live in etalii-adp/etalii.adp and are bundled, never edited here. `c4/code` keeps its registration and its refusing factory and gets no definition (Requirement 2.7). - Splices, never reserialization: the commands keep today's line surgery in this stage, which already changes one line and nothing beside it. The stricter FBL rule arrives with the second stage. - The four gates, the transcript and "a test seen to fail first" are the checks of every step. ### Project Structure (structure.md) - A diagram type adds declarations and no core code. What the libraries lack is added to `EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Disl` and to the client's `canvas/library/disl` for every tool (*Library work*), named for what it does. - The module gains `definition/` with six bundled definitions; the test project gains `Parity/`. ## Code Reuse Analysis ### Existing Components to Leverage - **`BundledDefinition.Load(assembly, logicalName, plugins)`**: loads one embedded `.dis` and reads its provenance from the resource `.provenance.json`. It already takes a name per definition, so six definitions need six pairs of embedded resources and no change to this class. - **`WireIdMap.Of(specification, "x-c4")`, `ToolboxDerivation.Derive(specification, ids)`, `ContextMenuDerivation.Derive(specification, target, env, ids)`, `FormDerivation.Derive(specification, element, env, ids)`, `ConstraintEvaluator.Evaluate(specification, diagram, options)`, `OperationInterpreter.Run`, `DislIds.Fixed`**: used as `TimelineDefinition.cs` uses them. Each takes the specification as an argument, so choosing one of six is the caller's. - **`DislModelBuilder.From(FblModel, DislSpecification)`** with hand-made `FblElement` records, as `TimelineDisl.cs` does: this is how a model is built from the module's own parser. `DislConstraintOptions.WrittenId` and an element's `HostAttributes` carry what the parser read and the metamodel does not hold. - **Derived relations** (`DislModelBuilder.DerivedRelations`): `from`, `source`, `target`, `id`, `sources` and `attributes` are computed. `key` is refused (see *Amendment proposed*, 1). - **The timeline's `Parity/` folder** (`TimelineTranscript.cs`, `TranscriptText.cs`) and the hype cycle's `HandWrittenGhg.cs` and `GhgRuleSet.cs` kept under `Parity/`: the generator, the comparison and the place of the oracle are copied in shape. - **`ContextTarget.Origin`**: a context target already carries its origin, so a provider can find the definition without a new seam. - **`parseDisl`, `compileNotation`, `NotationBindings`** (client library) and the `cylinder` member of `BuiltInShape`. - **`bundle-disl.sh`**: extended, not replaced (step 4). ### Integration Points - **etalii-adp/etalii.adp**: the six `definitions/diagrams/c4-*.dis` and their companions are rewritten there (step 2), through that repository's own pull request and checks. Step 4 cannot bundle before it is merged. - **`EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Fbl.Tests`**: untouched in this stage. The 33 entries of `RealFiles/divergences.json` are held against the vendored example binding and still occur, so they stay (Requirement 11.2). - **The other specifications of the series**: the library items below are shared. The requirements do not say which specification delivers one first, so each is delivered once, by whichever reaches it first, and the other finds it present. The ones most likely to be met elsewhere are L1 (`matchesGlob`), L5 (`location()`), L8 (several definitions for one module) and C1 (the `person` shape). ## Architecture ```mermaid graph TD Dis["definition/c4-*.dis
six, bundled, DISL 0.3"] --> Defs[C4Definitions
by origin] Dsl[".dsl body"] --> Parser[C4Parser
stays in this stage] Parser -->|C4Workspace| Adapter[C4Disl
stand-in for C1, C2, C6] Defs --> Adapter Adapter -->|"FblModel, views"| Builder[DislModelBuilder] Builder --> Model["DislDiagram
one per workspace and view"] Model --> Menus[ContextMenuDerivation / FormDerivation] Model --> Findings[ConstraintEvaluator] Findings --> Order[C4FindingOrder
stand-in for C10] Model --> Mapper[C4ElementMapper
members, lifted lines, title, legend] Menus --> Providers[the three providers, handing out] Providers -->|"today's commands"| Store[C4DocumentStore] ``` ### The steps | Step | What changes | Held by | Depends on | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | `Parity/c4.transcript.json`, its generator, one new fixture per finding marked Read, and the test that today's code reproduces it, seen to fail against a changed sentence. No product code changes. | Requirement 1 | Nothing | | 2 | In etalii.adp: the six definitions at DISL 0.3 with `language.origin`, `persistence.format: "fbl"`, `typeMap`, the id rule and `x-c4`; the six companions rewritten. | Requirements 2.1 to 2.4 | That repository's pull request | | 3 | Library work L1 to L9, each with a test seen to fail first. No module changes. | Requirements 10.1, 10.2, 10.5 | Step 2, whose definitions name what is called | | 4 | `bundle-disl.sh` bundles several definitions for one module; the six are bundled and embedded; `C4Definitions`; `BundledDefinition.Tests` with the comparison of the shared layers. Nothing derives yet. | Requirements 2.3, 2.5, 2.6, 2.7 | Steps 2 and 3 | | 5 | `C4Disl`. Toolbox, menus and rows derived; the three providers hand out; their logic moves to `Parity/HandWrittenC4.cs`. | Requirements 3.1, 3.2, 3.6, 3.7 | Step 4 | | 6 | The two empty-canvas labels end in an ellipsis, by bundling the definition revision that states them so. The transcript changes in those two labels only. | Requirement 3.8, finding A14 | Step 5 | | 7 | Findings derived by `ConstraintEvaluator` and ordered by `C4FindingOrder`; `C4Validator` becomes a call to it. | Requirement 3.3 | Step 5 | | 8 | The mapper and the layout take a view's members, its lifted lines, its interactions, its title and its legend from the model. `C4RuleSet` moves to `Parity/`. | Requirements 3.4, 3.5, 3.7 | Step 7, Amendment 1 | | 9 | The client compiles its canvas definition from the bundled definition of the view's kind; client library work C1 to C3; today's definition stays in a test as the oracle; the `tests.md` entry. | Requirement 9 | Step 4 | | 10 | The companions' table of remaining classes and of gaps; documentation and catalog; the delivery report. | Requirements 8.3, 11.1, 11.3 to 11.5, 12 | Steps 5 to 9 | Step 6 is a step of its own so that the only transcript difference of this stage has one cause. Steps 5, 7 and 8 each replace one hand-written part, so a difference names the part. Reading does not change in any step: `C4Parser` reads every body throughout, which is what lets a difference be attributed to derivation alone. ### Modular Design Principles - One concern per file: the definitions, the adapter, the order of findings, the mapper and the layout are separate classes. - The providers hold no logic: each finds the entry and the view, and calls `C4Definitions`. - No module name enters a library; no library type is subclassed by the module. ## Components and Interfaces ### C4Definitions - **Purpose:** the six bundled definitions and what is derived from them. - **Interfaces:** `For(DiagramOrigin)`; `For(C4ViewKind)`; `Toolbox(origin)`; `Menus(workspace, view, elementId)`; `Rows(workspace, view, elementId)`; `Problems(workspace)`; `Diagnostics`. - **Dependencies:** `EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Disl`. - **Reuses:** the shape of `TimelineDefinition`; the table of origins and view kinds that `ServiceCollection.AddC4.cs` holds today moves here. - **Which definition answers** (Q6, default): the toolbox is the origin's, as `C4ToolboxProvider` is constructed per origin today. A menu, a row and a drawn line are derived from the definition of **the view's own kind**, whatever the registration's origin, because the module draws a view by its kind today. A target with no view (a registration whose `view:` names nothing) uses the origin's definition and an empty model. - **Findings are the model's, not a view's.** `C4RuleSet.Validate` takes the workspace and no view, so every rule is `over: "model"` and all six validators give the same list. Requirement 2.3 holds the constraint layer equal in all six, so the validator of any origin evaluates its own definition and the transcript holds the six lists equal. - **A menu target** is an element, a stored relationship, or the empty canvas. A drawn line that is not a stored relationship is a derived relation without `edits`, for which the derivations return nothing (finding A10); an unknown id returns nothing. ### C4Disl (the stand-in of Q5) - **Purpose:** the DISL model of a `C4Workspace` for one view. - **Interfaces:** `Of(workspace, view)` cached per parsed workspace and view key, as `TimelineDisl.Of` caches per parsed model; `Build(workspace, view)` for an operation to change; `ElementOf(diagram, wireId)`. - **Ids.** A node's model id is the identifier the parser gives, which is today's wire id; one the declaration did not write (`__`, finding A8) is marked not stored, so the definition's `missing: "ephemeral"` applies to it and nothing is written into the `.dsl` (Q7). A stored relationship's model id is today's `->@` (finding A7), also marked not stored. Lookups compare without case through L4. - **A dangling relationship** is built with a null end and the written identifiers kept as host attributes, as the timeline keeps `writtenFrom` and `writtenTo`, so the definition's own rule reports it once, with its line, and `std.references` is switched off (findings A13, B8; Q4). - **The view's statements** become the diagram's attributes (`includes`, `excludes`, `title`, `autoLayout`, `rankSeparation`, `nodeSeparation`, `scope`, `environment`) and a dynamic view's interactions become `Interaction` elements. This is the half of the reading FBL cannot do yet (finding B13). - **Every view** of the workspace is handed to the model as a view (L3), with its own attributes, so that a model-wide rule can ask `diagram.views`. - **Why code:** gaps C1, C2 and C6 stop the binding from reading what the tool reads. The class is named in the companions as standing in for them. ### C4FindingOrder (the stand-in of Q4) - **Purpose:** today's order: the includes, then per element its findings in rule order, then the relationships, then each view, then coverage. - **Interfaces:** `Order(findings, workspace)`. - **Why code:** `constraints.order` orders by code and then by line (`ConstraintEvaluator.Ordered`), which cannot state "by element" (gap C10). `TimelineDefinition.Problems` does the same for the timeline with a table of groups. ### The providers, the validator, the mapper and the commands - **`C4ToolboxProvider`, `C4ContextActionProvider`, `C4ContextPropertyProvider`:** hand out `C4Definitions.Toolbox`, `.Menus` and `.Rows`. A label that follows state ("Add description…" and "Edit description…") is the definition's CEL Message. Executing an action still builds today's command: the definition's operation gives the prompt, the refusal and the new element's attributes, and the command writes, as the timeline maps its operations onto its commands. - **`C4Validator`:** `C4Definitions.Problems(workspace)`. - **`C4ElementMapper`, `C4Layout`:** the four calls of `C4RuleSet.MembersOf` become a read of the view's members from the model (L2). A stored relationship is drawn when both its ends are members and keeps its menu. A relationship with an end that is not drawn is drawn as the derived `LiftedRelationship`, whose id is the lifted ends with the first source's line (L5, and `key` for the merge). The two never share an id, which matters because `DislModelBuilder` refuses to draw a derived element whose id a stored one has. The synthetic ids `c4:view` and `boundary:` stay the mapper's. - **Commands, `C4Placement`, `C4LayoutSidecar`, `C4DocumentFactory`:** unchanged in this stage. A new element's identifier stays `C4Placement.IdentifierFor`, handed to the operation through `DislIds.Fixed`, which settles finding A9 for now: the definition declares `natural` with the pattern and the suffix, and the identifier made from a name is host code named for gap C11. ### The client - `C4Canvas.tsx` imports the six bundled `.dis` files with `?raw` and compiles the one of the view's kind: `compileNotation(parseDisl(text), C4_BINDINGS)`. The card's three labels, the fitted type line and the wrapped description are stated in the notation; what the library cannot read is added to the library (C1 to C3), never written here (Requirement 9.3). - The title band and the legend keep arriving in the `c4:view` payload, which the backend now fills from the definition (L7), so the wire does not change. ## Library work (Requirement 10) Each item is added with a test seen to fail first, and no module name appears in it. The list is a reading of the definitions as they must be rewritten and is **confirmed by loading the six rewritten definitions at the start of step 3**: the loader names every function and construct it refuses, and that output replaces this list where they differ. The searches were made in `src/backend/EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Disl`, sources only. | # | What | Evidence that it is missing | | --- | --- | --- | | L1 | `matchesGlob(s, glob)` in `DislCelLibrary` (DISL 12.4). | Searched for `matchesGlob`: none. The twelve declared methods do not include it. | | L2 | A viewpoint's `include`, `exclude` and `members`, answered as a view's members. | Searched for `"members"`: one hit, the expression walker's list of keys. Nothing evaluates it. | | L3 | Views on `DislDiagram` (`id`, `viewpoint`, `name`, `members`, and the diagram attributes of that view), `diagram.views`, and a constraint's `over`. | Searched for `"over"` and `diagram.views`: none. Searched `Model/DislDiagram.cs` for `Views`: none. | | L4 | `ids.compare: "ignore-case"` for lookups, references and duplicates, and `ids.missing`. | Searched for `ignore-case`, `"compare"` and `"missing"`: none. | | L5 | `location()` on an element, from the line the reader gave it. | Searched for `location`: one hit, a key name in the expression walker. `DislElement.Line` exists and is what it returns. | | L6 | A derived relation's `key`: items grouped, one relation per group, `group` bound to the members. | `DerivedRelations` answers a declaration with `key` by the finding "groups its items by key, which this runtime does not compute yet". | | L7 | The canvas's header Message and its legend computed from what is drawn (DISL 6.13), answered on the backend. | Searched for `"legend"` and `"header"`: a context name, a walker key and an unrelated `typeMap` case. Nothing derives either. | | L8 | Several definitions for one module: the bundle script takes definition names and writes one provenance file beside each; a small `BundledDefinitionSet` loads them and finds one by `language.origin`. | `bundle-disl.sh` copies `definitions/diagrams/.dis` and one `provenance.json`. Searched the library for `"origin"`: none. | | L9 | Whatever `ConstraintEvaluator` lacks for a rule that reports once per relationship with a missing end and takes its line from `location()`. | To be shown by the fixture `dangling-both-ends.dsl` at step 3. | Not built: the runtime does not resolve `imports`, and stays so, because Q8 stands at six self-contained files (Requirement 10.3). `EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Fbl` is not changed in this stage (Requirement 10.4 waits). Client library, in `src/client/src/canvas/library`: | # | What | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | | C1 | A `person` shape, and `cylinder` and `person` in the DISL shape catalog. | `BuiltInShape` has `cylinder` and no `person`. `disl/shapeCatalog.ts` names eight shapes, neither among them. | | C2 | A node that ignores gestures (the dashed boundary), stated in the notation. | Today a comment in `C4Canvas.tsx` says the flag is set on the element by hand. To be confirmed by compiling at step 9. | | C3 | What `compileNotation` lacks for three stacked card labels with a fitted line and a wrapped block. | To be confirmed by compiling at step 9; `labels.ts` already wraps a declared label. | ## Data Models ### The parser's reading and the metamodel | `C4Parser` gives | Becomes | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | `C4Element` of the eight kinds | Node types `Person`, `SoftwareSystem`, `Container`, `Component`, `DeploymentNode`, `InfrastructureNode`, `ContainerInstance`, `SoftwareSystemInstance` | `name`, `description`, `technology`, `tags`, the parent, and `of` for an instance. The line is the element's `Line`. | | `C4Relationship` | Relation `Relationship` | Ends resolved by the parser; a missing end is null with the written text as a host attribute. | | `C4Interaction` of the view | `Interaction`, and from it the derived numbered line | Only the shown view's, as today. | | `C4View` (each) | A view of the model (L3) | `key` as the id, the kind as the viewpoint. | | `C4Workspace.Includes` | `IncludedFile` | No viewpoint draws it; a rule gives today's sentence, without a location (finding B11, Q4). | | `styles` | Nothing | Kept as today: recorded and not read (finding A15). | `std.duplicateId` is switched off in the definitions (Q4): two elements of one identifier are both read and the first is the one an edit finds, as today. ### The transcript One JSON file, `Parity/c4.transcript.json`, shaped as the timeline's: `module`, `generator`, `regenerate`, then per origin the `toolbox`, then `documents`. Per document: `findings` once, and per view `menus` (every element, every drawn line, the empty canvas, an unknown id), `rows`, `payloads`, and `edits` (every command once, with each step's answer and the hunks it made to the body and to the sidecar). A document whose bytes equal an earlier one is written as `sameAs` it. Nothing an edit makes is random, so nothing is masked. ## Amendment proposed **1. Finding A5 and Requirement 10.1: a derived relation's `key`.** A5 says "Derived relations are implemented". They are, without grouping: `DislModelBuilder.DerivedRelations` answers a declaration that has `key` with a finding and derives nothing. Requirement 3.4 needs it, because several relationships that land on one drawn pair are one line that keeps the first one's line. The options, to be put to the user as a selection: - **Add "a derived relation's `key`" to the list of Requirement 10.1 and correct the last sentence of A5** (recommended: it is a count and a sentence, the work is library work of the kind 10.1 already holds, and this design lists it as L6). - Leave 10.1 as it is and keep the merge in `C4ElementMapper`, named as standing in for a runtime gap. Requirement 3.4 is then met for the lines that are not merged only. - Other. This design is written against the first. **2. Requirement 2.2 under the default of Q5: the binding a definition names.** Requirement 2.2 has each definition name the module's binding by URL. Requirement 4.1, which creates that file, waits with the rest of Requirement 4. Between the two stages the six definitions would name a file that is not there. The options: - **The module's binding is committed in step 4, in the state FBL 0.2 can express** (findings B1, B2, B8, B10, B11 and B23 repaired, none of the six keys the appendix marks as not FBL 0.2), embedded, held by a test that loads it without an error, and on no reading path (recommended: the definitions then name a real file, and the second stage starts from a binding that already loads). - The definitions name the URL and the file arrives with the second stage. Nothing here resolves the URL, so nothing fails; a reader of the definition finds a dead link. - Other. This design is written against the first. It brings the first sentence of Requirement 4.1 forward and nothing else of Requirement 4. ## What waits, and on what | What | Requirements | Waits on | | --- | --- | --- | | The body read through the binding; `C4Disl` deleted; `C4Parser`, `C4Tokens` and `C4Document` leave the product code. | 4.2 to 4.7, part of 8.2 | etalii.adp: C1 (the selected view's statements), C2 (a comment after a brace or a statement), C6 (an unbalanced body). C3 and C4 for the fixtures that show them. | | Every edit by splices; `C4Placement` and the commands' line surgery leave; the template's bytes. | 5, part of 8.2 | The reading above; C4 (an escape), C5 (positional optional arguments). The transcript's edit hunks are then regenerated once (Q1). Finding B19 is fixed there with its guard. | | Several readings through one open FBL body; the view chosen by the registration header. | 6.1 to 6.4 | The reading above; C7 for a `view` that names nothing. Until then these hold because the store, the session factory and the registration reading are not touched, which the transcript and `C4SharedRead.Tests` show. | | Positions as FBL 8.7 says; `C4LayoutSidecar` leaves; finding B17; the refusal of Q7. | 7, part of 8.2 | The reading above; C7 for the number form and the comparison of keys. | | FBL library work and its conformance fixtures; the 33 divergences removed. | 10.4, 11.2 | Each language change, vendored from etalii.adp. | The second stage keeps the rule of the first: the binding is embedded and read beside the parser first, then reading switches, then writing, then positions, each a pull request held to the same transcript. Findings B17 and B19 need no language change; whether they are brought forward is the user's to rule, and this design leaves them with their requirements. ## Error Handling ### Error Scenarios 1. **A bundled definition does not load, or its bytes are not those its provenance names.** - **Handling:** `C4Definitions` throws on first use with the loader's diagnostics; `BundledDefinition.Tests` fails in the gate. - **User Impact:** none in a released build. 2. **The six definitions drift apart in a shared layer.** - **Handling:** the comparison of Requirement 2.3 fails in the gate and names the layer and the two files. - **User Impact:** none. 3. **A derived relation cannot be computed** (`std.derivedFailed`, `std.derivedEnds`, `std.derivedId`). - **Handling:** a test requires none over the whole corpus. At run time the finding is logged and not reported, because the tool gives no such finding today (Requirement 3.3, Q4); the line is not drawn. - **User Impact:** a line missing, with the reason in the log. Each such case found is a defect to repair in the definition. 4. **A registration's `view:` names no view.** - **Handling:** as today: an empty canvas and a line in the log (Requirement 6.3). The origin's definition gives the toolbox. - **User Impact:** unchanged. 5. **An operation refuses** (an empty name, a kind that may not stand under that parent, a name already taken). - **Handling:** the definition's refusal is compared with the command's sentence in the transcript; the command still refuses on its own, so a stale menu cannot write. - **User Impact:** the sentence shown today. 6. **The transcript differs after a step.** - **Handling:** the step is not delivered, unless it is step 6 and the difference is the two labels. - **User Impact:** none. ## Testing Strategy ### Unit Testing - Library: one test class per item L1 to L9, each seen to fail before its change. L6 has the cases of DISL 4.11.3: two items on one pair, the first one's attributes, the `sources` of the group. - `C4FindingOrder`: a document with a finding of every code, interleaved so that the order is pinned. - `BundledDefinition.Tests`: for each of the six, the embedded bytes equal `definition/`, the recorded sha256 holds, the definition loads with no error; and the six shared layers are equal as parsed data. - The guard of finding A14: a test that requires the ellipsis, seen to fail against the `&` at step 5 and passing from step 6. ### Integration Testing - **The transcript test** is the main one: every step must reproduce the checked-in file byte for byte. - **Derived against hand-written**, per kind, as the hype cycle's `Parity/` has: toolbox, menus, rows, findings, drawn lines, each comparing `C4Definitions` with `HandWrittenC4` over the corpus and all its views, so a difference names the document, the view and the element. - **One fixture per finding marked Read** (Requirement 1.2), among them `lenient-spellings.dsl` (B6), `block-comments.dsl` (B5), `trailing-comments.dsl` (B4), `escaped-quote.dsl` (B7), `nested-relationships.dsl` (B8), `tags-in-block.dsl` (B9), `misplaced-container.dsl` (B10), `unbalanced.dsl` (B22), `view-without-key.dsl` (B2), `unidentified-elements.dsl` (A8), `dangling-both-ends.dsl` (A13), `autolayout-ignores-positions.dsl` with a sidecar (A12), and edit scripts for B17, B18, B19 and B20. A finding that does not show is struck by a small amendment (Requirement 11.5). - The existing store, session, layout, interop and shared-read tests stay and pass unchanged. The providers' and the rule set's own tests move with their subjects to the oracle, each accounted for in the tasks. ### End-to-End Testing - The `tests.md` entry of Requirement 9.4, in a real browser, in both themes. - A newly created worktree is built before the gates are trusted, at steps 4, 6 and 9, because each changes what is embedded or imported from `definition/`. ## What remains in the module after this stage, and why | Class | Stays because | | --- | --- | | `C4Layout`, `C4Metrics`, `C4Theme` | The definition names the layout as a plugin (finding A16); a view's `autoLayout` reaching it is gap C9. `C4Theme` stays where the notation does not replace it. | | `C4ElementMapper`, `C4Session`, `C4SessionFactory`, `C4DocumentStore`, the reloader, `C4ContextSourceResolver` | Payloads, the viewport filter and the shared document lifecycle are the host's. | | `C4Disl` | Gaps C1, C2 and C6 (Q5). | | `C4FindingOrder` | Gap C10 (Q4). | | `C4Parser`, `C4Tokens`, `C4Document`, `C4Placement`, the commands, `C4LayoutSidecar`, `C4DocumentFactory` | The second stage (*What waits*). `C4Placement.IdentifierFor` also stands in for gap C11. | | `AddC4ViewCommand`, `RemoveC4ViewCommand` | Gap C8 (Requirement 6.5). | | `C4CodeDocumentFactory`, `C4StructurizrMirror` | `c4/code` refuses on purpose; the mirror is a table the interop tests read. | `C4RuleSet`, `C4Rules` where the definitions carry the codes, and the logic of the three providers are in `Parity/` after step 8. ## Requirement Coverage | Requirement | Where | | --- | --- | | 1 | Step 1; *The transcript*; Testing Strategy | | 2 | Steps 2 and 4; *C4Definitions*; L8; Amendment 2 | | 3 | Steps 5 to 8; *C4Definitions*, *C4Disl*, *C4FindingOrder*, the mapper; L1 to L7; Amendment 1 | | 4 | 4.1 in step 4 (Amendment 2); the rest in *What waits* | | 5 | *What waits*; unchanged commands meanwhile | | 6 | 6.5 in *What remains*; 6.1 to 6.4 held unchanged, then *What waits* | | 7 | *What waits* | | 8 | 8.1 and 8.3 in *What remains* and step 10; 8.2 for the rule set and the providers in steps 5 to 8, the rest in *What waits* | | 9 | Step 9; *The client*; C1 to C3 | | 10 | Step 3; *Library work*; 10.3 not built (Q8); 10.4 in *What waits* | | 11 | Step 10; *Integration Points* (the divergences stay); fixtures per finding; both stand-ins named | | 12 | Step 10; End-to-End Testing (the fresh worktree) |
